corpus: MEASURED 2026-09-20, live: 8 of 30 libraries resolve to a genuine full-text llms-full.txt doc (drizzle-orm, prisma, trpc, zod, hono, bun, vite is llms-full.txt too but see note, convex, openai, vitest, sveltekit, nuxt, vue, resend - see `sources`); most of the rest resolve to an llms.txt that is itself an index of links with no prose (next.js, react, supabase, shadcn, stripe, ai-sdk, expo's own llms-full.txt is ALSO index-shaped despite the name, clerk, anthropic-sdk, tanstack-query, motion); a few fall back to a raw GitHub README or a single docs-repo page because the registry's llms-full.txt/llms.txt candidates 404 live (tailwindcss, firebase, playwright, react-router, astro). This eval script (like D-27's original design) ranks ONLY the primary document it fetches - it does not follow index links the way get_docs does - so an index-only primary document honestly yields `expect: []` for most of its questions even though the real answer may exist on a page get_docs would follow into (see PAR-844/PAR-845 for that separate, real mechanism). A low top-1 hit rate here is the expected, honest result of that architecture plus many primary documents genuinely being indices, not a retrieval defect.
labellingRule: A section counts as correct when a developer asking that question would be materially helped by that section's own text: it names the API or concept asked about and shows or explains it. A word appearing in a feature bullet, a link list, a sponsor list, a repository-directory listing, or an unrelated context (a support-policy table, a test-harness setup) does NOT count. Where no section of the fetched document meets that bar, `expect` is [] and `unanswerable` is true: the question is still one of the 60, and neither ranker can score it. Labelled from the documents' own headings and text, before either ranker was run against them - the same rule the 2026-09-06 labelling used, applied fresh against the new corpus rather than carried over.
matching: Each regex in `expect` is tested (case-insensitively, JavaScript RegExp) against the top-ranked section's rendered heading path - ancestors joined with ' > ', the section's own heading last. A question is a hit when any regex matches.
